entries.title: Mark 7:1
segments: One day the Pharisees came to him in a body with some Scribes who had come from Jerusalem.

entries.title: Mark 7:2
segments: They had noticed that some of his disciples were eating with "common," that is to say, unwashed hands.

entries.title: Mark 7:3
segments: For the Pharisees and all of the Jews do not eat until they have ceremoniously washed their hands in obedience to the tradition of the elders;

entries.title: Mark 7:4
segments: and when they come from the market-place they do not eat without bathing first: and they have many other customs which they have received and observe, such as the washing of cups and jugs and copper pans.

entries.title: Mark 7:5
segments: So the Pharisees and Scribes asked him: "Why do your disciples not follow the traditions of the elders? Why do they eat with 'common' unwashed hands?"

entries.title: Mark 7:6
segments: "Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, hypocrites," he answered. "As it is written, @"This people honor me with their lips, While their hearts are far from me;

entries.title: Mark 7:7
segments: But in vain do they worship me, For their teaching is only human precepts.@

entries.title: Mark 7:8
segments: "You neglect the commandment of God, and hold fast the traditions of men."

entries.title: Mark 7:9
segments: "It is praiseworthy, is it," he exclaimed, "to reject the command of God that you may keep your tradition!

entries.title: Mark 7:10
segments: For although Moses said, @Honor your father and mother, and Let him who curses father or mother suffer death@,

entries.title: Mark 7:11
segments: you say that if a man tells his father or mother, 'This money which otherwise you would have received from me, is Korban' (that is, a thing devoted to God),

entries.title: Mark 7:12
segments: you exempt him from doing any service for his father or mother.

entries.title: Mark 7:13
segments: Thus by your tradition which you have handed down you set at naught the word of God; and you do many other things like that."

entries.title: Mark 7:14
segments: Then again he called the crowd to him and said:

entries.title: Mark 7:15
segments: "Listen to me, all of you, and understand; there is nothing outside a man which by entering in can defile him; but it is what comes from him that defiled him."

entries.title: Mark 7:17
segments: After he had left the crowd and gone indoors his disciples began asking him about the parable.

entries.title: Mark 7:18
segments: "Are even you without understanding?" he said. "Do you not perceive that nothing whatever from without can defile a man by entering him,

entries.title: Mark 7:19
segments: because it does not go into his heart, but into his belly, and passes away, ejected from him?" By these words he pronounced all foods clean.

entries.title: Mark 7:20
segments: "What comes out of a man," he continued, "is what defiles him.

entries.title: Mark 7:21
segments: From within, from the heart of man, proceed evil purposes--

entries.title: Mark 7:22
segments: fornication, theft, murder, adultery, greed, malice, deceit, wantonness, envy, slander, arrogance, reckless folly--

entries.title: Mark 7:23
segments: all these wicked things issue from within and defile a man."

entries.title: Mark 7:24
segments: After he rose and left that place, he went away into the region of Tyre and Sidon. Here he went into a house and wished no one to know it but he could not be hid.

entries.title: Mark 7:25
segments: Forthwith a woman whose little daughter was possessed by an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet

entries.title: Mark 7:26
segments: (the woman was a Greek, a Syro-phoenician by race), and again and again she begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

entries.title: Mark 7:27
segments: "Let the children be filled first," he said to her. "It is unseemly to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."

entries.title: Mark 7:28
segments: "True, Master," she answered, "but the dogs under the table do pick up the children's crumbs."

entries.title: Mark 7:29
segments: "For that saying of yours, go home," he replied; "the demon has departed from your daughter."

entries.title: Mark 7:30
segments: So she went home, and found the child lying in her bed and the demon departed.

entries.title: Mark 7:31
segments: Again he left the region of Tyre, and passed through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, crossing the District of the Ten Towns.

entries.title: Mark 7:32
segments: And they brought to him a deaf man who stammered, and begged him to lay his hands upon him.

entries.title: Mark 7:33
segments: So Jesus took him aside from the crowd, by himself, and put his finger in the man's ears, and moistened his tongue with saliva;

entries.title: Mark 7:34
segments: then looking up to heaven with a sigh, he said to him, "Ephphatha!" (that is, "Be opened.")

entries.title: Mark 7:35
segments: And his ears were opened and the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke plainly.

entries.title: Mark 7:36
segments: Then Jesus charged them not to tell any one, but the more he charged them, the more they published it;

entries.title: Mark 7:37
segments: and people were amazed beyond measure saying: "How successfully he does things! Even the deaf he makes to hear, and the dumb to speak."
